title: Allocator fencing and ephemeral KV leak remediation (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: Multiple production escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments surfaced a correlated failure mode: an allocator race that allows short-lived KV handles to become orphaned during concurrent session teardown. Over time this causes micro-fragmentation in GPU slab arenas and eventual OOM spikes under bursty inference workloads. The issue appears in workloads that mix long-sequence chat sessions with many short single-token requests (prefix/poke traffic patterns).

Impact: Customer-visible OOMs leading to request failures and degraded latency on both Hosted and Dedicated pools; Private/on-prem customers reported repeated pod restarts and manual node reboots. Escalations from three customers (company anonymized) and internal SRE alerts triggered an emergency investigation.

Repro and root cause hypothesis: Repro steps created in lab: 1) Run mixed-concurrency harness with 60% short requests (<=8 tokens) and 40% long requests (>=512 tokens) targeting the same session IDs. 2) Enable session eviction and aggressive KV compaction. 3) Observe KV handle refcounts dropping to zero while allocator metadata still references slab segments.
Root cause: a race between session-eviction callback and the slab allocator's free path where ephemeral KV entries are cleared in two phases. If a concurrent request rebinds the session during the window between soft-free and final reclamation, a dangling pointer path leaves small orphaned allocations that frustrate coalescing heuristics. These micro-fragments accumulate under heavy churn and eventually exhaust contiguous allocation units on some GPU memory managers.

Temporary mitigations applied: - Deployed an emergency flag that disables aggressive KV compaction on affected pools to slow fragmentation progression. - Enabled per-session eviction backoff to reduce simultaneous frees. - Applied conservative request admission controls on high-risk Hosted clusters to preserve capacity for in-flight long requests.

Long-term fix plan: 1) Allocator fencing: add a lightweight per-session fence that serializes the final KV reclaim path with session rebinds. This prevents races without full stop-the-world pauses. 2) Ephemeral-KV auditer: runtime shim that tracks short-lived KV entries and opportunistically drains or migrates them to a small slab pool to avoid polluting large arenas. 3) Slab coalescer improvements: make coalescing tolerant of small transient handles and add background compaction windows tuned to workload phases. 4) Rollout: start with Canary in Hosted cluster zone us-west-2a (low-risk customers), then expand to Dedicated pools with traffic shaping, finally to Private with an opt-in agentized patch. 5) Add a runtime feature flag and automated rollback if OOMs or tail latency regress.

Monitoring and success criteria: - Track contiguous-free-chunk histogram in allocator (target: reduce 95th percentile fragmentation by 70% in canary). - OOM incidents per cluster (target: zero new OOMs related to allocator path during canary). - Customer error rate on affected endpoints (target: <0.1% increase). - Post-rollout stability window: 14 days at Canary, 7 days for Dedicated, 30 days for Private.

Artifacts and links: - Root cause doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime/ENG-101210-root-cause (internal) - Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/allocator-frag/ENG-101210 - Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11234 - Runbook (emergency steps): https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/allocator-oom-playbook - Repro harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rc-harness/tree/eng-101210
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Raman: Initial triage call with SRE and oncall. Captured three customer incidents and correlated them against allocator metrics. Created repro harness under eng-101210 branch.

2026-03-11 - Daniel Cho: Confirmed deterministic repro in lab with mixed short/long workload. Observed per-GPU contiguous chunk exhaustion. Began prototype of per-session fence and small-slab pool for ephemeral entries.

2026-03-12 - Mei Alvarez (SRE): Deployed temporary mitigation flags to affected Hosted pools; alerts dropped but several Dedicated clusters still saw elevated memory churn. Notified customers of in-flight mitigations and ETA for permanent fix.

2026-03-13 - Daniel Cho: Opened hotfix PR (11234) implementing allocator fencing with unit and stress tests. PR includes a runtime flag and metrics exports. Preparing canary plan; requested review from @Katherine Patel and @Ravi Singh.
2026-03-13 - Katherine Patel (Tech Lead): Reviewed patch; suggested reducing fence granularity to per-session-window to limit impact on throughput. Added performance test to CI matrix.
